# Crazy Putt Arena

Crazy Putt Arena is an original browser-based arcade mini-golf game built with TypeScript, Three.js, Rapier 3D and Vite. The target product is a full match: one human player against configurable bot opponents across themed holes, with mouse aiming, a charged power meter, arcade-tuned ball physics, a scoreboard between holes, and a rating and progression update at the end.

The project is mid-assembly. Most systems are implemented as separate, unit-tested modules under `src/`, but they are not wired into a playable loop yet. Read [Current state](#current-state) first: what `npm run dev` opens today is a menu over an empty 3D scene, not a playable hole.

## Current state

What happens today when the app runs:

- `src/main.ts` creates a Three.js renderer, an empty scene, a perspective camera and the HTML UI layer above the canvas, then starts a render loop.
- `AppUI` (`src/ui/index.ts`) renders the menu and navigates between the main screen, Quick Play / Ranked / Custom setup, Settings and Profile. The profile numbers are placeholder data and the settings form keeps its values in memory only.
- **Start Match** reads the setup form and calls an optional `startMatch` callback. `src/main.ts` passes no callbacks, so no match starts.
- There is no ball, hole geometry, aiming line, power meter, bot turn, scoreboard or rating update in the browser yet. A production build transforms about 20 modules; the rest of `src/` is not referenced from the entry point.

Implemented and unit-tested, but not reachable from the running page yet:

| Area | Modules |
| --- | --- |
| ball physics and shots | `src/physics` (`helpers`, `ShotSystem`, `GolfBallPhysics`, `PhysicsWorld`, `CollisionLayers`) |
| obstacles | `src/obstacles` (rotating parts, movers, bumper/spring/boost/jump pads, conveyors, fans, teleporters, surface friction) |
| hazards and force fields | `src/gameplay/zones` (water, lava, kill, magnet, gravity) |
| match flow | `src/gameplay` (`MatchManager`, `TurnManager`, `HoleSystem`, `ScoreManager`, `RatingSystem`, `MatchRewards`, `StateMachine`) |
| bots | `src/ai` (`BotPlanner`, `BotProfiles`, `BotTurnScheduler`, `Matchmaking`) |
| camera | `src/camera` (controller, modes, smoothing, transitions, collision avoidance) |
| courses | `src/courses` and `src/courses/data` (10 courses x 9 holes), `src/core/HoleSceneBuilder` |
| player data | `src/player` (profile, progression, cosmetics), `src/core/SaveManager` |
| in-game HUD | `src/ui` (`Hud`, `Scoreboard`, `Overlays`, `Minimap`) |

The next step is assembling these in the entry point: build the hole scene, run the physics step, route input into a shot, drive the turn order and mount the HUD.

## Requirements

- Node.js 20 or newer (checked on 24.8)
- A modern desktop browser with WebGL 2 (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari)

## Install

```bash
npm install
```

## Run

```bash
npm run dev
```

Vite prints a local URL (http://localhost:5173 by default); open it in the browser. You land on the menu described in [Current state](#current-state).

## Build

```bash
npm run build
```

The build type-checks the project with `tsc -b` and then emits the bundle into `dist/`.

## Typecheck

```bash
npm run typecheck
```

## Test

Two test runners are in use and there is no aggregate `npm test` script yet.

### Vitest

Vitest covers the suites that sit next to the code in `src/`, plus `tests/course-data-validation.test.ts` (validates 10 courses x 9 holes) and `tests/physics/helpers.test.ts`. The package scripts each run one slice:

```bash
npm run test:ui      # src/ui - 2 files, 11 tests
npm run test:input   # src/input and src/dev - 2 files, 5 tests
npm run test:camera  # src/camera - 3 files, 32 tests
```

The whole vitest set runs with:

```bash
npx vitest run
```

Right now 26 files (166 tests) pass and 3 files are reported as failures. All three are runner mismatches rather than broken code:

| File | Why vitest fails on it |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/leaderboard-generator.test.ts` | written for `node:test`, so vitest reports no test suite found |
| `tests/leaderboard-render.test.ts` | same |
| `tests/save-manager.test.mjs` | imports from `../.test-build/`, which no script produces |

### node:test

The two leaderboard suites pass under the Node runner:

```bash
node --test tests/leaderboard-generator.test.ts tests/leaderboard-render.test.ts
```

They import TypeScript sources directly, so Node 22.18+ or 24 is required.

### Not runnable yet

`tests/save-manager.test.mjs` imports `SaveManager`, the player profile and the progression curve from a compiled `.test-build/` directory. No npm script emits that directory, and a plain `tsc --outDir .test-build` emit is not sufficient because the emitted ESM imports carry no file extensions. Until an emit step (or extension-safe imports) is added, this suite cannot be executed as committed.

## Project structure

All gameplay code lives under `src/`:

| Folder | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `app` | top-level game state shape |
| `ai` | bot planners, bot profiles, turn pacing, matchmaking and skill rating |
| `assets` | asset and audio managers with graceful fallbacks |
| `camera` | camera controller, modes, smoothing and collision avoidance |
| `config` | tunable game configuration values |
| `contracts` | shared types for events, math, services and zones |
| `core` | renderer, scene manager, hole scene builder and save manager |
| `courses` | course builder, hole model and the course data sets |
| `dev` | launch options, diagnostics overlay and presentation minimap |
| `effects` | particle effects |
| `gameplay` | match flow, turns, scoring, rating, rewards, state machine and zones |
| `input` | keyboard, mouse and touch-ready input handling |
| `leaderboard` | leaderboard model, generator and styles |
| `obstacles` | rotating parts, movers, pads, conveyors, fans, teleporters, surfaces |
| `physics` | physics world, ball physics, shot system and collision layers |
| `player` | player profile, progression and ball cosmetics |
| `ui` | menu shell, HUD, overlays, scoreboard, minimap and DOM helpers |

Only `config`, `input`, `ui` and (behind the debug flag) `dev` are currently reached from `src/main.ts`.

## Debug flags

URL flags are parsed by `src/dev/LaunchOptions.ts`:

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `?debug=1` | lazy-loads `src/dev` and mounts the diagnostics overlay (FPS, frame time, draw calls, triangles, camera position) |
| `?course=<id>` | parsed and written to `document.documentElement.dataset.debugCourse`; it does not load the course yet |
| `?hole=<n>` | parsed the same way into `dataset.debugHole`; it does not start a hole yet |

Course ids present in `src/courses/data`: `green-hills`, `pirate-bay`, `candy-factory`, `ancient-temple`, `arctic-base`, `volcano`, `neon-city`, `haunted-mansion`, `space-station`, `chaos-dimension`.

Example: `http://localhost:5173/?debug=1&course=volcano&hole=4` shows the overlay and records both values in the DOM dataset. Starting that hole is part of the gameplay loop that is not assembled yet.

Hotkeys, active only while the diagnostics overlay is loaded:

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `F1` | show or hide the diagnostics overlay |
| `F2` | toggle wireframe materials on the scene |
| `F3` | show or hide the developer presentation minimap (`src/dev/PresentationMinimap.ts`); the in-game minimap in `src/ui/Minimap.ts` is not mounted yet |

## Audio assets

`public/audio` holds the placeholder structure for sound. No audio binaries are committed: `public/audio/manifest.json` lists every audio event the game can play, using the definition shape consumed by `src/assets/AudioManager.ts` (`id`, `url`, `category`, `volume`, `loop`, `optional`). Every entry is marked optional, so the AudioManager treats a missing file as a non-fatal fallback and the game simply runs silently.

To enable sound, drop `.mp3` files into `public/audio/<category>/<id>.mp3` matching the manifest entries. See `public/audio/README.md` for the folder layout, the entry format and the naming rules.

## Known gaps

- The entry point does not assemble the gameplay loop: no hole scene, physics step, shot input, turn order or HUD.
- `?course` and `?hole` are recorded in the DOM but start nothing.
- Menu settings and the profile screen show placeholder data and are not persisted through `SaveManager`.
- There is no aggregate test script, and `tests/save-manager.test.mjs` cannot run until its `.test-build/` emit exists.
- No audio binaries ship with the repository; the game runs silently by design.
